definition: Directing a model toward a target behaviour by intervening on its internals at inference. The two sources here differ in scope: one builds multi-layer steering vectors from sparse-autoencoder features selected by co-activation and decoder-direction alignment, reporting it as the only method that consistently preserves fluency where single-point interventions fail entirely on sycophancy and refusal; the other places steering as the intervention half of a Locate-Steer-Improve pipeline categorized by the interpretable object being acted on. Neither tests steering on reasoning itself, so whether a reasoning process is steerable the way an attribute like toxicity is remains open in this archive.

evidence.note: Builds multi-layer steering vectors from SAE features selected by co-activation and decoder-direction alignment, and intervenes at several points instead of one.
evidence.title: CircuitSteer: Geometrically Aligned Multi-Layer Steering via Sparse Autoencoder Circuits

evidence.note: A survey reorganizing mechanistic interpretability from observation into a Locate-Steer-Improve intervention pipeline, categorized by the interpretable object being acted on.
evidence.title: Locate, Steer, and Improve: A Practical Survey of Actionable Mechanistic Interpretability in Large Language Models

name: steering
